A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CrossNovo study. Text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison; the reordered appendices and checklist can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original peptide-sequencing experiments, component ablations, beam-size analyses, antibody evaluations and PTM fine-tuning results in Tables 1–8 and accompanying figures.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental outcomes, including the antibody and PTM results in the relocated appendices.

M1.justification: The shared encoder, AT/NAT decoders, CE/CTC objectives, importance annealing, cross-decoder attention and gradient blocking are unchanged. Algorithm 1 and the appendix PMC decoding procedure are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use MassIVE-KB, 9-species-v1/v2, human and mouse antibody datasets, and the 21-PTM dataset with the same five reported modifications. Appendix relocation introduces no additional coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout. Table 2 retains PrimeNovo, CasanovoV2 and ContraNovo; antibody Tables 6–7 retain CasanovoV2 and ContraNovo; PTM Table 8 retains PrimeNovo. Table 1's broader baseline set also matches.

E3.justification: Training configurations, mass-based matching thresholds, beam-size settings, zero-shot antibody evaluation and PTM-specific fine-tuning remain unchanged. No additional or revised evaluation protocol is reported.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same beam-size analyses in Tables 3 and 5, component ablations in Table 4, similar-mass amino-acid analysis in Figure 3 and appendix cross-attention alignment analysis.

E5.justification: Checklist item 7 states in both versions that each primary experiment was conducted once because of cost. Neither version reports additional seeds, uncertainty estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: All eight tables and the result plots retain their entries and findings. CrossNovo's average AA precision/peptide recall remains 0.811/0.654 on 9-species-v1 and 0.906/0.786 on 9-species-v2; appendix antibody and PTM scores also match.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations in Section 3 and Appendices A.2–A.3 are unchanged, including the CTC independence assumption and forward recursion, and PMC's mass constraint and dynamic program. No theorem or proof is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same hybrid AR–NAR contribution and performance claims. Removing the peptide-sequencing subtitle does not change the stated contributions or experimental scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning bidirectional context, gradient interference, target leakage, beam-size effects and downstream generalization are retained. Appendix A.1 preserves the same limitation concerning incomplete phylogenetic coverage.

D1.justification: Architecture hyperparameters, optimizer and learning-rate schedule, GPU disclosure, antibody data-handling details and appendix decoding documentation are unchanged. The GitHub and anonymous code-link destinations also match.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Wei et al.'s 2023 study on identifying blue horizontal branch stars and additional citations to existing AR/NAR-related references. The added ICML RefineNovo entry matches its already cited preprint. The central research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 removes 'Application in De Novo Peptide Sequencing' from the title, alphabetizes the references and moves the checklist before the scientific appendices. The main prose and appendix explanations remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is smaller, Figure 2's caption gains bold emphasis, and title typography and spacing change. Appendix Tables 5–8 and Figure 5 move with the appendices; their displays and scientific content are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves the same scientific evidence, mathematical detail, reproducibility information and limitations, including all eight tables and the single-run disclosure. The limited citation, title and layout edits do not resolve a substantive deficiency or meaningfully alter the paper's overall quality.
